skill.name: cypress-author

skill.summary: Authors reliable Cypress tests for new behavior, changed requirements, and failing or flaky coverage.

content.value_statement: Writing stable Cypress tests requires project context, framework knowledge, and careful command usage. This skill creates, updates, and repairs tests using established project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests as creating, updating, or fixing Cypress tests.
Infers end-to-end or component testing from configuration, file paths, and framework context.
Reviews Cypress configuration, support files, package metadata, and related tests.
Creates or edits Cypress specifications while matching project language and conventions.
Applies stable selectors, explicit assertions, reusable setup, network interception, and Cypress command chains.
Checks configured formatting, linting, and compilation requirements after changes.
limitations: Supports Cypress tests only and does not author tests for alternative frameworks.
Requires a target specification, testing type, and clear behavior before authoring.
Does not run tests unless the user explicitly requests execution.
May need Cypress documentation or project CLI information for version-specific commands.

use_cases.title: Add Journey Coverage
use_cases.description: Create end-to-end coverage for a new user journey while reusing existing setup and selector conventions.

use_cases.title: Repair Unstable Tests
use_cases.description: Replace arbitrary waits and fragile selectors with retryable assertions, aliases, and controlled network behavior.

use_cases.title: Test UI Components
use_cases.description: Create isolated component tests for React, Vue, or Angular behavior using the project's mounting patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Cypress test for [behavior] in [spec path]. Use the existing project conventions and tell me whether it is E2E or component testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a focused test from a clear behavior and target file.

prompt_templates.title: Extend Existing Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [spec path] to cover [new behavior]. Reuse existing helpers, preserve test independence, and add explicit assertions for [expected outcome].
prompt_templates.scenario: Add coverage to an established Cypress specification.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Flaky Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix the flaky test at [spec and test name]. Investigate waits, selectors, shared state, asynchronous logic, and network timing before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Repair unstable coverage without changing the tested behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor Cypress tests in [scope]. Consolidate repeated setup, preserve isolated execution, align selectors with project priorities, and verify configured quality checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve maintainability across several related tests.

output_examples.input: Create an E2E test for invalid login attempts in the existing login specification.
output: Updated the existing login specification instead of creating a duplicate file.
Added an isolated invalid-login scenario with explicit validation assertions.
Reused the project's stable selectors and reset application state before the test.

output_examples.input: Fix a test that waits five seconds before checking search results.
output_examples.output: Replaced the fixed delay with a network alias and a retryable result assertion. The test now waits for observable application behavior.

output_examples.input: Add component coverage for a React button with loading and disabled states.
output_examples.output: Added focused component scenarios for loading and disabled states using the project's mount helper and accessible element queries.

best_practices: Provide the target specification, testing type, expected behavior, and relevant failure details.
Keep tests independent and prepare application state before each scenario.
Use stable selectors, retryable assertions, and network aliases instead of fixed delays.
anti_patterns: Do not request Cypress changes without identifying the affected behavior or specification.
Do not depend on state created by another test or a previous test run.
Do not store Cypress command results in variables or mix command chains with unmanaged Promises.

faq.question: Can this skill create both E2E and component tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies the testing type from your request, file paths, configuration, and framework context.

faq.question: Can it update an existing Cypress specification?
faq.answer: Yes. It prefers extending a relevant existing specification when that matches the requested behavior.

faq.question: Does it run the tests after editing?
faq.answer: Only when you explicitly request test execution. It otherwise focuses on authoring and configured quality checks.

faq.question: How does it address flaky tests?
faq.answer: It checks selectors, shared state, fixed waits, network timing, and incorrect asynchronous patterns.

faq.question: Does it support JavaScript and TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It follows the project's existing language, formatting, and Cypress type patterns.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the target behavior, specification path, testing type, and any expected outcome or failure details.
